newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Ferrell FX Index up 0.7 pct in November.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Ferrell FX Index up 0.7 pct in November.

text.p: The Ferrell FX Index rose 0.7 percent in November with the median return flat, Ferrell Capital Management said on Thursday.
Twenty-three of 35 programs reported positive results in November, Ferrell said.
Friedberg Commodity Management Inc, of Toronto, turned in the top performance for the third straight month, reporting gains of 9.7 percent.
"During November we established a short Swiss franc position vis-a-vis the long British pound," Friedberg vice president Rick Zauderer told Ferrell.
Advanced Trading Strategies Ltd, of Dublin, placed second with gains of 6.0 percent. And Baltimore-based Campbell & Co came in third with returns of 5.8 percent.

"The story for the month continues to be the strength of (sterling), which has appreciated against a stronger U.S. dollar and a weaker basket of European currencies," said Ferrell president William Ferrell.
"The market seems to be paying the pound respect for staying out of the European Monetary Union and the related uncertainty about (EMU's) initial constituency and start-up date," he added.
For the 119-month period from January 1987 through November 1996, the compounded annual return of the Ferrell FX Index is 17.8 percent.
The index provides a benchmark for multi-advisor currency portfolios and includes 37 programs managed by 32 firms in the United States, United Kingdom, France, Canada, Ireland and Switzerland.
